analysis:
Docs-only PR: docs/developer/test.md (head lines 177-207) adds an opt-in live test, ModelCheckpointRestoreContentionLiveTests, for SSD restore TTFT contention. docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md (head line 119) adds a 'Provider-staged destinations' row describing zero-host-byte staging that skips eval/stream fences so it avoids MLX evalLock. Date stamps were bumped. There is no code change, so no executable security regression is visible here.

Security-relevant observations for later passes:
- The test uses an isolated ephemeral cache and a minimal env (env -i). It is explicit about not using production cache roots or keys. This is consistent with T-041 and the cross-tenant timing-oracle concerns; it reports TTFT and staging timing across tenants but does not weaken any control. The report is written to a caller-chosen path and contains timings and samples, not content.
- The ssd-kv-cache.md row describes a behavior change in the provider-staged import path (CheckpointHostZeros.swift, CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift, PagedCheckpointStorage.swift, CompleteCheckpointImportPlan.swift). It charges the largest destination as staging scratch because the zero source can briefly commit memory outside the MLX allocator. The implementing code is not in the supplied batch, so memory-admission accounting accuracy (availability, T-029/T-016-adjacent) and whether zeroed destinations are fully overwritten before use (T-028 residual data) remain unverified. The correctness of the described behavior should be checked against the source changes if a code batch exists.
- Removing eval/stream fences might alter the timing observable by other tenants (T-041 oracle). That is a claim about docs, not evidence of regression.
No threat-model update is strictly required. TB-011, TB-002 and the attestation assets are untouched.
